key_insight: Neutral oxygen vacancy formation energies in binary main-group metal oxides are largely explained by two bulk descriptors: crystal reduction potential and band gap.
engineering_relevance: The model can help screen oxide materials for vacancy-sensitive energy applications without explicit defect calculations, though solar-cell performance was not evaluated.
method: Survey 39 binary oxide polymorphs using r²SCAN density functional theory.
Use ShakeNBreak to locate reconstructed defect ground states.
Fit an interpretable model using pristine-bulk properties.
evidence_signal: Formation energies span 8 eV, and the two-descriptor model achieves a held-out mean absolute error of 0.31 eV.
watch_item: Accuracy may degrade where vacancy electrons are accommodated through mechanisms other than cation reduction.
paper_title: Periodic Trends in Oxygen Vacancy Formation Energies Across Binary Main-Group Metal Oxides
